meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (root 'нести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to carry to', forming an aspectual pair with 'относить'.

examples.text: Они сами себя на склад не отнесут!
examples.trans: They will not carry themselves to the storeroom!

examples.text: Покушай спокойно, пока я отнесу ящики внутрь.
examples.trans: Eat calmly while I carry the crates inside.

examples.text: Я отнёс часть продуктов на наш склад.
examples.trans: I carried part of the groceries to our storeroom.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'already'.

examples.text: Я уже десять минут жду, имейте совесть!
examples.trans: I have been waiting ten minutes already, have a conscience!

examples.text: И жизнь меня за это уже наказала.
examples.trans: And life has already punished me for that.

examples.text: Подожди, Арсений, Баринов уже завтра отсюда уйдёт.
examples.trans: Wait, Arseny, Barinov will leave here tomorrow already.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'ten', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже десять минут жду, имейте совесть!
examples.trans: I have been waiting ten minutes already, have a conscience!

examples.text: Я дам тебе десять процентов от заказа!
examples.trans: I will give you ten percent of the order!

examples.text: Через десять минут.
examples.trans: In ten minutes.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'minute', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я уже десять минут жду, имейте совесть!
examples.trans: I have been waiting ten minutes already, have a conscience!

examples.text: Будет готово ровно через две минуты, Шеф!
examples.trans: It will be ready in exactly two minutes, Chef!

examples.text: Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Мы с нетерпением вновь ждём встречи с ним.
examples.trans: We eagerly look forward to meeting him again.

examples.text: Я уже десять минут жду, имейте совесть!
examples.trans: I have been waiting ten minutes already, have a conscience!

examples.text: Леночка, дорогая, жди меня сегодня к четырём.
examples.trans: Lenochka, darling, wait for me today by four o'clock.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to have'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я уже десять минут жду, имейте совесть!
examples.trans: I have been waiting ten minutes already, have a conscience!

examples.text: Имей совесть!
examples.trans: Have a heart!

examples.text: Вы имеете право молчать.
examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'conscience', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я уже десять минут жду, имейте совесть!
examples.trans: I have been waiting ten minutes already, have a conscience!

examples.text: Имей совесть!
examples.trans: Have a heart!

examples.text: У него нет совести.
examples.trans: He has no conscience.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Иди скорее, Денис, прими свежие продукты.
examples.trans: Go quickly, Denis, accept the fresh groceries.

examples.text: Почему именно я должен идти на склад?
examples.trans: Why do I have to be the one to go to the storeroom?

examples.text: Если так нужно, иди на улицу налови!
examples.trans: If you need them so badly, go catch some on the street!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'faster'.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее на студию!
examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

examples.text: Скорее да, чем нет.
examples.trans: Rather yes than no.

examples.text: Тащи скорее прищепку!
examples.trans: Bring the clothespin quickly!

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.en: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to receive', forming an aspectual pair with 'принимать'.

examples.text: Ну как, Денис, ты принял все продукты?
examples.trans: Well how is it, Denis, did you accept all the groceries?

examples.text: Спасибо, что принял меня.
examples.trans: Thanks for seeing me.

examples.text: Она примет вас завтра.
examples.trans: She'll see you tomorrow.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.text: Почему именно я должен идти на склад?
examples.trans: Why do I have to be the one to go to the storeroom?

examples.text: Интересно, почему меня не позвали на разговор?
examples.trans: Interesting, why was I not invited to this conversation?

examples.text: Нет, почему же, я делаю это осознанно.
examples.trans: No, why not, I am doing this consciously.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('exactly') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему именно я должен идти на склад?
examples.trans: Why do I have to be the one to go to the storeroom?

examples.text: Гости пришли сюда есть именно мою еду!
examples.trans: The guests came here to eat my food specifically!

examples.text: Именно для этого дела мы все созданы.
examples.trans: It is for this very craft that we were all created.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'must', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Почему именно я должен идти на склад?
examples.trans: Why do I have to be the one to go to the storeroom?

examples.text: Настоящего мужчины всегда должно хватать на всех!
examples.trans: There should always be enough of a real man for everyone!

examples.text: Ты должен ударить меня ещё два раза.
examples.trans: You are supposed to kick me two more times.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно ты, ведь это обязанность всех новеньких!
examples.trans: Of course you, after all that is the duty of all newcomers!

examples.text: Конечно едят, ведь это дорогая французская дичь!
examples.trans: Of course they eat them, after all it is expensive French game!

examples.text: Конечно, сейчас вам подадут его луковый суп!
examples.trans: Of course, right now they will serve you his onion soup!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Конечно ты, ведь это обязанность всех новеньких!
examples.trans: Of course you, after all that is the duty of all newcomers!

examples.text: Витя, ну брось обижаться, ты взрослый человек!
examples.trans: Vitya, stop sulking, you are a grown man!

examples.text: Я ведь пришёл к тебе по делу.
examples.trans: After all, I came to you on business.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('after all') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно ты, ведь это обязанность всех новеньких!
examples.trans: Of course you, after all that is the duty of all newcomers!

examples.text: Конечно едят, ведь это дорогая французская дичь!
examples.trans: Of course they eat them, after all it is expensive French game!

examples.text: Я ведь пришёл к тебе по делу.
examples.trans: After all, I came to you on business.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('this') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Мне вот за работу досталось это пианино.
examples.trans: I ended up with this piano for my work.

examples.text: Я подумаю об этом в понедельник.
examples.trans: I will think about that on Monday.

examples.text: Я же заранее предупреждала вас об этом.
examples.trans: After all, I warned you about this in advance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (root 'язанность'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to all'.

examples.text: Конечно ты, ведь это обязанность всех новеньких!
examples.trans: Of course you, after all that is the duty of all newcomers!

examples.text: Сеня, я плачу совсем не из-за лука.
examples.trans: Senya, I am not crying because of the onion at all.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: И со всеми артистами расплатились странными вещами.
examples.trans: And they paid all the performers with strange things.

examples.text: Мы недавно обедали у вас, всё понравилось.
examples.trans: We had lunch at your place recently, we liked everything.

examples.text: Все были в восторге от Виктора Баринова!
examples.trans: Everyone was delighted with Viktor Barinov!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'new girl', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Конечно ты, ведь это обязанность всех новеньких!
examples.trans: Of course you, after all that is the duty of all newcomers!

examples.text: Новенькая, наверное.
examples.trans: She must be new.

examples.text: Познакомьтесь, это наша новенькая официантка в зале.
examples.trans: Meet her, this is our new waitress in the dining room.
